subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram provider intermittently stalls despite stable direct Bot API connectivity

question: Should OpenClaw fix this through a shared scheme-aware proxy contract that covers both explicit and environment SOCKS/HTTP/HTTPS proxy modes, or should maintainers wait for stronger live Telegram SOCKS proof before choosing the proxy behavior?
rationale: The source and Undici contract make the SOCKS path plausible, but the remaining repair changes compatibility-sensitive shared proxy behavior and the open candidate PR is partial and unproven.

options.title: Sponsor shared proxy repair
options.body: Require a replacement or updated patch that covers explicit and env proxy modes, preserves HTTP/HTTPS proxy defaults, adds focused regression tests, and includes redacted live Telegram proof.

options.title: Request live diagnostics first
options.body: Keep this issue open but wait for a current-main SOCKS5 getMe/sendMessage transcript before approving a shared proxy behavior change.

options.title: Limit to documentation/workaround
options.body: Treat current config and DNS/proxy guidance as sufficient until a maintainer accepts new proxy behavior or a stronger reproducible failure appears.

recommendation.title: Sponsor shared proxy repair
recommendation.body: Require a replacement or updated patch that covers explicit and env proxy modes, preserves HTTP/HTTPS proxy defaults, adds focused regression tests, and includes redacted live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows the strongest overlap with shared proxy helper and recent Telegram transport diagnostics work.
